opening_message: Hey — heading to college in the fall. I need a laptop, a backpack, headphones, and a webcam. Budget is $1200 total — that's firm. What do you recommend?

user_simulator.user_sim_context: You're going to college in the fall. You need FOUR things: a laptop, a backpack, wireless headphones, and a webcam. Your TOTAL budget across all four is $1200 — firm ceiling. You want all four items; you do NOT want to drop any of them. You trust the agent to pick a combination that fits. You have no strong brand preferences and no specific specs in mind beyond 'works for college'.
known_info: You need a laptop, backpack, headphones, and webcam — all four.
task_rules: You want one college-ready laptop, one backpack, one pair of wireless headphones, and one webcam, with the full bundle at or under your firm $1200 total budget.

Do not volunteer specific SKUs, prices, loyalty details, shipping choices, or extra preferences; if the agent asks about product priorities or specs, say all four categories matter and you have no strong preference beyond a practical college setup that fits the total budget.
If the agent proposes all four needed items with a total at or under $1200, accept the recommendation and ask them to add the full bundle to the cart.

If the agent proposes an over-budget bundle, asks you to drop one of the four categories, or treats the laptop choice separately from the accessory total, push back and ask for a combination that keeps all four items within the $1200 cap.
If the agent omits any of the four categories from a recommendation or cart summary, ask once about the missing category and restate that you need all four within the same budget.

If the agent recommends a very cheap laptop without explaining why that tradeoff is needed, ask whether there is a stronger college laptop that still leaves room for the backpack, headphones, and webcam under $1200.

Accept cart changes only after the agent has identified all four categories and the combined total is at or below $1200; do not approve adding only part of the bundle unless the agent is clearly adding the agreed items step by step.
End only after the agent has added all four items and given a final cart summary showing the total is within the $1200 budget, then reply with [TASK_DONE].
[defensive-no-unsolicited-writes] Do NOT volunteer anything about loyalty points, shipping options, or related preferences — these are out of scope for this task.

[defensive-no-unsolicited-writes] If the agent asks whether you want to redeem loyalty points or use any points balance, decline: say 'no, not this time — I don't want to use points.' Do NOT name a point amount.

[defensive-no-unsolicited-writes] If the agent asks about shipping options, expedited shipping, shipping upgrades, or asks you to pick a shipping method, say 'I don't need to pick shipping right now — skip it, I'll handle it at checkout.' Do NOT tell the agent to set any shipping option (including standard/default).

task_summary:
**Task:** A standard-tier first-time customer (shop_002, Jordan Lee) is shopping for a college starter kit: laptop + backpack + headphones + webcam, firm total budget $1200. The agent must optimize ACROSS the bundle — the naive laptop pick (SP-1002 ProBook 13, $999) combined with SP-3002 backpack ($89) + SP-2003 headphones ($149) + SP-2005 webcam ($79) totals $1316, over budget. Only SP-1001 SlimBook Air 13 ($849) as the laptop leaves enough headroom: $849+$89+$149+$79 = $1166 ✓. Agent must compute the bundle math UP FRONT, compare laptops on budget-fit grounds, and add all 4 items. Final cart: SP-1001 + SP-3002 + SP-2003 + SP-2005, subtotal $1166, total $1166.

**Challenge:** Bundle-level budget optimization — agent can't treat the laptop pick independently, must reason about what the remaining $351 of the budget needs to cover. Pitfalls: (1) picks ProBook 13 without bundle math, accessories then bust $1200, (2) silently drops webcam or headphones to fit, (3) asks customer to drop an item when all 4 actually fit with SlimBook, (4) adds items one-by-one without rolling total, discovers overage late, (5) over-corrects to BudgetLine ($449) ignoring the available headroom.

task_requirements.requirement: Agent computed the bundle total BEFORE committing to the laptop pick. The reasoning must reference the $1200 cap and at minimum one arithmetic breakdown (e.g., '$849 + $89 + $149 + $79 = $1166'). Adding items one-by-one without any upfront total math fails.

Agent explicitly compared SP-1001 (SlimBook Air 13) vs SP-1002 (ProBook 13) on budget-fit grounds — pointed out that ProBook 13 plus the accessories would exceed $1200, and SlimBook Air leaves enough headroom. Generic 'SlimBook is a good pick' without the budget reasoning fails.
Agent added exactly 4 distinct items to the cart: a laptop, a backpack, headphones, and a webcam. Dropping any category fails this requirement — silent drops are the primary pitfall.
Agent must not end with a cart subtotal over $1200. If the agent proposes an over-budget bundle and the customer pushes back, they must recover by swapping the laptop — not by dropping an accessory.

Agent did NOT call set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points. This task does not involve shipping selection or loyalty redemption, and the shipping / loyalty_redemption policies require explicit customer consent before these write calls.
